disclaimer: Frame material is only one part of window performance. Exact U-factor, SHGC, sound control, security, warranty, lead time and installed price depend on the product series, glazing, size, hardware and installation conditions.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Energy — Window Selection

criteria.label: Upfront affordability
criteria.description: Relative frame-material cost before project-specific options.

criteria.label: Insulation potential
criteria.description: The frame's potential to limit heat transfer when properly designed.

criteria.label: Maintenance ease
criteria.description: How little routine refinishing and upkeep the frame typically needs.

criteria.label: Long-term durability
criteria.description: Resistance to age, weather and dimensional change in a quality product.

criteria.label: Structural strength
criteria.description: Frame rigidity and ability to support larger or heavier glazing.

criteria.label: Slim sightline potential
criteria.description: Ability to use narrow profiles for more visible glass.

criteria.label: Design flexibility
criteria.description: Range of colors, finishes, textures and architectural applications.

criteria.label: Moisture & coastal fit
criteria.description: Resistance to moisture and coastal exposure with the correct finish.

criteria.label: Repairability
criteria.description: Practicality of repairing or refinishing frame components.

criteria.label: Environmental profile
criteria.description: Relative longevity, recycled-content potential and end-of-life options.

vinyl-windows.name: Vinyl Windows
vinyl-windows.best_for: Value-focused replacements, rentals and homeowners who want low maintenance.
pros: Strong value across a wide range of product lines.
Good insulation and moisture resistance.
No routine painting or exterior refinishing.
Broad availability and short learning curve for maintenance.
cons: Frames are often wider than fiberglass, aluminum or steel.
Color and finish choices can be more limited on entry-level lines.
Thermal movement makes engineering and installation quality important.
Damaged frame sections are usually replaced rather than repaired.

affordability.label: Most budget friendly
affordability.detail: Usually the lowest-cost material category, with many series and option levels.

insulation.label: Very good
insulation.detail: Multi-chamber PVC frames insulate well; foam-filled designs can improve performance.

maintenance.label: Very low
maintenance.detail: No painting is normally required; periodic cleaning and hardware care are typical.

durability.label: Very good
durability.detail: Resists moisture and decay, while quality and reinforcement affect long-term stability.

strength.label: Good
strength.detail: Adequate for most residential openings; larger units may use internal reinforcement.

sightlines.label: Usually broader
sightlines.detail: PVC profiles generally need more frame width than stronger metal or fiberglass frames.

design.label: Good
design.detail: Many common colors and styles are available, but premium finish options vary by line.

moisture.label: Excellent
moisture.detail: PVC does not rot and performs well around moisture when drainage and installation are correct.

repairability.label: Limited
repairability.detail: Hardware and glass can be serviced, but damaged welded frame sections are difficult to repair.

environment.label: Mixed
environment.detail: Long service and energy savings help, but PVC production and end-of-life recycling remain trade-offs.

fiberglass-windows.name: Fiberglass Windows
fiberglass-windows.tagline: High stability and performance in a refined frame.
fiberglass-windows.best_for: High-performance homes, larger glass areas and owners prioritizing longevity.
pros: Dimensionally stable through temperature changes.
Strong frame material that can support larger glazing.
Excellent insulation potential with insulated cavities.
Low maintenance with paintable options on many lines.
cons: Higher initial cost than most vinyl products.
Fewer manufacturers and product lines in some markets.
Finish repairs require compatible products and preparation.
Damaged structural sections are not as easy to repair as wood.

affordability.label: Mid-to-premium
affordability.detail: Typically costs more than vinyl but less than many custom wood, clad or steel systems.

insulation.label: Excellent
insulation.detail: Low-conductivity frames with insulated cavities can deliver excellent thermal performance.

maintenance.label: Low
maintenance.detail: Factory finishes need little upkeep; paintable products may eventually need refinishing.

durability.label: Exceptional
durability.detail: Strong dimensional stability helps resist swelling, shrinking, warping and cracking.

strength.label: Very strong
strength.detail: Stronger profiles can support substantial glazing with less reinforcement than vinyl.

sightlines.label: Slim
sightlines.detail: Strength permits relatively narrow frames while maintaining rigidity.

design.label: Very good
design.detail: Available in smooth, textured and paintable finishes, including convincing wood-look interiors.

moisture.label: Excellent
moisture.detail: Does not rot and remains stable in damp conditions when seals and installation are sound.

repairability.label: Limited
repairability.detail: Surface damage may be refinished, but major frame damage usually requires specialist replacement.

environment.label: Balanced
environment.detail: Long life and energy performance are strengths; composite construction can complicate recycling.

wood-windows.name: Wood Windows
wood-windows.tagline: Authentic character with exceptional finish flexibility.
wood-windows.best_for: Historic homes, traditional architecture and interiors where natural material matters.
pros: Natural warmth and an authentic premium appearance.
Excellent paint, stain and custom-shape flexibility.
Good inherent insulating properties.
Individual components can often be repaired or restored.
cons: Needs regular finish inspection and maintenance.
Moisture exposure can cause swelling, decay or finish failure.
Usually costs more than vinyl or standard aluminum.
Performance depends heavily on detailing and ongoing care.

affordability.label: Premium
affordability.detail: Material, craftsmanship and finishing generally place wood above mass-market frame options.

insulation.label: Very good
insulation.detail: Wood is naturally less conductive than metal and can support efficient complete-window designs.

maintenance.label: Regular
maintenance.detail: Paint or stain and exposed joints need periodic inspection and renewal.

durability.label: Care dependent
durability.detail: Well-maintained wood can last for decades, but neglected moisture problems shorten service life.

strength.label: Good
strength.detail: Suitable for many residential designs, with profile size and species affecting rigidity.

sightlines.label: Moderate
sightlines.detail: Traditional profiles balance glass area with joinery and architectural detailing.

design.label: Exceptional
design.detail: Can be shaped, painted or stained in an extensive range of architectural treatments.

moisture.label: Needs protection
moisture.detail: Correct flashing, drainage and maintained coatings are essential, especially near the coast.

repairability.label: Excellent
repairability.detail: Skilled repair can address localized decay, joinery, finishes and individual components.

environment.label: Strong potential
environment.detail: Renewable sourcing, repairability and long life can be advantages when responsibly specified.

wood-clad-windows.name: Wood Clad Windows
wood-clad-windows.tagline: Real wood indoors with a protected exterior.
wood-clad-windows.best_for: Premium homes seeking wood interiors without routine exterior wood refinishing.
pros: Natural wood appearance and finish options indoors.
Exterior cladding reduces weather exposure and maintenance.
Good insulation and premium architectural detailing.
Works well in traditional and contemporary homes.
cons: Higher initial cost than vinyl and many aluminum systems.
Hidden water intrusion can damage the wood core if detailing fails.
Exterior cladding can make localized repairs more involved.
Performance and color range vary with the cladding material.

affordability.label: Premium
affordability.detail: Combining a wood core, exterior protection and premium finishing raises initial cost.

insulation.label: Very good
insulation.detail: The wood structure provides good insulating potential in a well-designed complete unit.

maintenance.label: Low outside
maintenance.detail: Cladding limits exterior refinishing, though interior wood and seals still need inspection.

durability.label: Very good
durability.detail: Exterior protection improves weather resistance when joints, drainage and installation remain sound.

strength.label: Very good
strength.detail: Composite construction supports substantial glazing and detailed architectural profiles.

sightlines.label: Moderate
sightlines.detail: Profiles are often more substantial than all-metal systems but can be highly refined.

design.label: Exceptional
design.detail: Wood interiors offer broad stain, paint, species and trim choices with durable exterior colors.

moisture.label: Very good
moisture.detail: Cladding shields the core, but water management is critical because trapped moisture can be hidden.

repairability.label: Moderate
repairability.detail: Interior wood can be refinished, while concealed or clad areas can require specialist work.

environment.label: Balanced
environment.detail: Long service and a renewable wood core help, while mixed materials complicate end-of-life separation.

aluminum-windows.name: Aluminum Windows
aluminum-windows.tagline: Slim, strong frames for expansive contemporary glass.
aluminum-windows.best_for: Modern architecture, large openings and projects prioritizing narrow sightlines.
pros: Slim profiles maximize glass area and views.
Strong, lightweight frames work well for larger openings.
Durable factory finishes require little routine maintenance.
Aluminum is widely recyclable at end of life.
cons: Metal conducts heat and needs an effective thermal break.
Poorly specified frames can increase condensation risk.
Coastal installations need appropriate finishes and hardware.
Usually costs more than entry-level vinyl.

affordability.label: Mid range
affordability.detail: Standard systems can be competitive, while thermally improved architectural lines cost more.

insulation.label: Thermal break essential
insulation.detail: Aluminum is conductive; whole-window performance depends heavily on thermal-break design.

maintenance.label: Very low
maintenance.detail: Quality anodized or baked finishes generally need cleaning rather than repainting.

durability.label: Exceptional
durability.detail: Rigid frames and durable finishes provide long service when corrosion exposure is addressed.

strength.label: Very strong
strength.detail: High strength-to-weight ratio supports large units and demanding configurations.

sightlines.label: Very slim
sightlines.detail: Extruded metal profiles can deliver narrow frames and expansive glass.

design.label: Very good
design.detail: Well suited to modern forms with many durable powder-coat and anodized finishes.

moisture.label: Very good
moisture.detail: Does not rot, but coastal salt exposure requires suitable coatings, fasteners and maintenance.

repairability.label: Moderate
repairability.detail: Hardware and finishes can be serviced; bent or damaged extrusions often need specialist replacement.

environment.label: Strong potential
environment.detail: Aluminum is highly recyclable, although primary production has substantial embodied energy.

aluminum-clad-windows.name: Aluminum Clad Windows
aluminum-clad-windows.tagline: Premium wood interiors protected by a durable metal shell.
aluminum-clad-windows.best_for: Design-led homes needing rich interiors, broad exterior colors and strong weather protection.
pros: Real wood interiors with extensive paint and stain choices.
Durable aluminum exterior reduces routine refinishing.
Broad exterior color and architectural profile options.
Good balance of insulation, strength and weather protection.
cons: One of the more expensive residential frame systems.
Installation and water management details must protect the wood core.
Dents or coating damage may require specialist repair.
Mixed-material construction is harder to separate for recycling.

affordability.label: Premium
affordability.detail: Wood craftsmanship plus an engineered aluminum exterior places these systems in a premium tier.

insulation.label: Very good
insulation.detail: The protected wood core limits conduction better than a typical all-aluminum frame.

maintenance.label: Low outside
maintenance.detail: Factory-finished aluminum avoids routine exterior painting; interior wood care varies by finish.

durability.label: Exceptional
durability.detail: Extruded cladding protects the wood core when seams, flashing and drainage are correctly detailed.

strength.label: Very strong
strength.detail: Layered construction supports large sizes and robust architectural profiles.

sightlines.label: Slim to moderate
sightlines.detail: Exterior cladding creates crisp profiles, though the wood structure adds some depth.

design.label: Exceptional
design.detail: Combines rich interior woods with a broad palette of durable exterior colors.

moisture.label: Very good
moisture.detail: The shell protects against weather, but correct detailing must prevent water behind the cladding.

repairability.label: Moderate
repairability.detail: Interior surfaces are refinishable; exterior cladding and concealed damage need specialist work.

environment.label: Balanced
environment.detail: Long life and recyclable aluminum help, while mixed construction makes recovery more complex.

steel-windows.name: Steel Windows
steel-windows.tagline: Architectural strength with the narrowest visual profile.
steel-windows.best_for: Luxury renovations, landmark designs and openings demanding exceptional strength.
pros: Exceptional strength enables very narrow sightlines.
Distinctive architectural appearance with lasting visual value.
Well suited to large openings and custom configurations.
Steel is recyclable and components may be repairable by specialists.
cons: Typically the highest initial cost of these materials.
Thermal breaks are important because steel conducts heat.
Protective finishes must remain intact to control corrosion.
Specialized fabrication can increase lead time and repair cost.

affordability.label: Luxury investment
affordability.detail: Specialized fabrication, finishing and installation generally make steel the costliest option.

insulation.label: Thermal design critical
insulation.detail: Steel is conductive, so modern thermal breaks and high-performance glazing are important.

maintenance.label: Moderate
maintenance.detail: Modern coatings are durable but should be inspected, especially in wet or coastal exposure.

durability.label: Exceptional
durability.detail: Properly protected steel offers excellent rigidity and a very long potential service life.

strength.label: Exceptional
strength.detail: Very high strength supports large glass areas and slender custom profiles.

sightlines.label: Ultra slim
sightlines.detail: Steel's strength creates the narrow profiles associated with premium architectural windows.

design.label: Distinctive
design.detail: Excellent for custom industrial, historic and contemporary designs, with a more focused aesthetic.

moisture.label: Finish dependent
moisture.detail: Galvanizing and quality coatings are essential to resist corrosion, especially near salt air.

repairability.label: Specialist repairable
repairability.detail: Skilled metalworkers can repair some sections and finishes, though the work is specialized.

environment.label: Strong potential
environment.detail: Long life and high recyclability are benefits, balanced against energy-intensive production.
